subject: PO-ID enforcement and mixed cadence billing proposal
messages:
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: samir.patel@aegishealth.com, apops@aegishealth.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PO-ID enforcement and proposed mixed cadence billing

Hi Samir / AP Ops,

Thanks for the productive call this morning. To keep procurement and finance aligned and avoid invoice routing delays, we'd like to propose a small set of enforceable PO metadata requirements and a flexible billing cadence that should fit Aegis' internal processes.

Key asks (proposal):
- PO-ID: required header format "PO-#####" (for AP matching). Please include on every PO line and on the top-level PO.
- Billing cadence: support a mixed cadence:
  - Weekly invoices for on-demand usage when monthly spend < $50k
  - Monthly consolidated invoices for larger, predictable commit blends
  - Quarterly consolidated PO/statement for enterprise-wide prepay/commit contracts
- Net terms: default to Net45 for billed usage; we can offer Net30 at a 4% discount and Net60 at -2% (i.e., reduced discount).
- Ledger mapping: billing entity and GL code must be present in PO header (we will map to the invoice for matching).

I've attached our billing profile for reference (redwood_billing_profile_v3.pdf). If you can share an example PO (Aegis format) we'll validate mapping on our side and provide a short amendment to the SOW to accept the cadence.

Next steps:
1) Samir/AP Ops: share a sample PO and confirm whether a single quarterly PO is acceptable as a master PO or whether finance requires per-month PO exchanges.
2) Redwood: will draft a proposed amendment outlining the cadence and the discount tiers for net terms and submit by end of week.

Thanks,

Jonas Weber
Director, Sales (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: PO-ID enforcement and proposed mixed cadence billing

Jonas,

Appreciate the clear proposal. A few clarifications from our side after running this by AP and Procurement:

- PO format: procurement can include PO-ID in the top-level header; however, our ERP requires a separate "Accounting PO" line for each billing entity. Will that break your invoice matching?
- Billing cadence: We prefer consolidated monthly invoices for operational simplicity. Weekly invoices are possible but will increase processing overhead on our side. Could we instead do monthly for usage and allow weekly only as an exception for pilot accounts?
- Net terms: Procurement is trying to standardize on Net60 across vendors. Can Redwood live with Net60 for the baseline? If not, can we trade longer terms for a smaller early-pay discount rather than a surcharge?

I've attached a sample Aegis PO export (Aegis_PO_Sample.xlsx) and a note from AP on their preferred GL field naming.

CC'ing AP Ops so they can confirm GL and accounting constraints.

Thanks,
Samir
Aegis Health — Procurement

Looping finance and sales ops thoughts here.

Ben / Kim — quick thoughts on options to propose back:

Option A (preferred buyer experience):
- Accept Net60 baseline (Aegis asks) but tie a small early-pay discount: Net30 = 5% vol discount; Net45 = 3% vol discount; Net60 = 0% discount.
- Accept quarterly master PO with monthly invoice statements submitted to AP using the PO-ID header for matching.
- For ERP mapping, we will support an "Accounting PO" line per billing entity; our invoicing pipeline can emit per-entity sub-lines to satisfy your ERP.

Option B (cost-optimized for Redwood):
- Require Net45 baseline as in initial ask, give 6% discount for Net30. Allow Net60 only with a 2% margin uplift.
- Offer ability to consolidate invoices monthly or quarterly depending on committed volume.

Operational asks to confirm before we commit:
- Exact GL field name (Samir/AP Ops said they'd send). We'll need a short mapping table.
- Whether AP can accept a single quarterly master PO as a top-level reference with monthly statements for matching (preferred) or if they require a separate PO per month.

I'll draft language for both options; Jonas, want me to send both to Samir and ask them to pick? Also should we include a clause to allow weekly pilot invoices for dev/test accounts under $5k/month so we don't over-index ops on either side?

Vanessa Ortiz
Head, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
